title: The Signal at Kestrel Station
author: Meanwhile Sample Stories
description: You are the only one awake at a research station on the ice when the radio starts saying your name.

media.description: Kestrel Station at night, a few windows lit against the snow.
media.label: Station at night (cover)

media.description: The station radio, its display pulsing with an incoming signal.
media.label: Radio pulsing

media.description: Three radio dishes in the snow, with footprints leading toward them.
media.label: Dishes with footprints

media.description: A pale dawn rising over the station.
media.label: Dawn over the station

media.description: Radio static with a faint repeating tone.
media.label: Static with tone

nodes.label: Opening: radio says your name
nodes.title: 2:14 a.m.
nodes.text:
The night shift at Kestrel Station is supposed to be quiet. Eleven people asleep, one generator humming, and you, alone in the radio room with a mug of coffee that went cold an hour ago.

Then the radio clicks on by itself.

Under the static, a voice. Calm, close, and saying your name. Twice. Then nothing but a soft three-note tone, repeating.

The nearest other station is four hundred kilometres away.

nodes.label: Waited: coordinates
nodes.title: 3:14 a.m.
nodes.text:
You don't move. You watch the display and count the tones until you lose count.

Exactly one hour after the first message, the voice comes back. It doesn't say your name this time. It reads out a string of numbers, slowly, the way you'd read them to someone writing them down.

You do write them down. When you check them against the station map, your pen stops.

The coordinates are for the antenna array, on the far side of the complex.

nodes.label: Walked: footprints
nodes.title: The long corridor
nodes.text:
You pull on your parka and take the connecting corridor toward the array. Halfway along, the lights flicker, and for a few seconds you walk in total darkness with one hand on the cold wall.

At the outer door you stop. The snow outside should be smooth; nobody goes out at night. But there is a line of footprints leading from the door toward the dishes.

They're your size. They're your boots.

And they're fresh.

nodes.label: Dormitory: Osei's note
nodes.title: An empty bunk
nodes.text:
Dr. Osei's bunk is empty. The blanket is folded and the sheets are cold, as if she got up hours ago.

Taped to her locker is a note in her handwriting:

"If the radio says your name, don't answer it. Come and find me. — A."

Down the corridor, faintly, the radio is still playing its three soft notes.

nodes.label: Array: meet Osei
nodes.title: The array
nodes.text:
You find Dr. Osei under the largest dish, her gloves off despite the cold, adjusting the receiver by hand.

"You came," she says, not looking up. "Good. I worked it out an hour ago. It's not coming from out there." She points at the sky, then at the station behind you. "It's coming from here. From us. Tomorrow night."

The receiver crackles. Your own voice, slightly tired, says: "If you can hear this, we need you to send it back."

nodes.label: Ending: never know (sleep)
nodes.title: Morning
nodes.text:
You go back to your bunk and lie awake until the day crew arrives. In daylight, the radio is just a radio. The log shows no transmissions at all.

You keep the page of numbers folded in your pocket for the rest of the season. You never find out what they meant.

Some nights, you're almost sure you can still hear three soft notes, very far away.

nodes.label: Ending: answer the radio
nodes.title: The answer
nodes.text:
You pick up the handset and say, "I'm here."

The static stops. In the silence, the voice speaks again, and this time you recognise it: it's yours, but older and very tired.

"I know," it says. "I always answer. That's the problem."

The line goes dead. Across the station, every light goes out.

nodes.label: Ending: send it back
nodes.title: The reply
nodes.text:
It takes the two of you the rest of the night. Osei rewires the transmitter; you read the message into the microphone over and over until your voice is steady.

At 4:00 a.m. you send it. The tone stops.

Tomorrow night, at 2:14 a.m., you'll be sitting in the radio room with a cold mug of coffee, waiting to hear yourself.

nodes.label: Ending: cut the power
nodes.title: Silence
nodes.text:
You find the junction box and pull the main breaker for the array. The dishes groan to a stop. The receiver goes quiet.

Osei stares at you for a long moment. "Then we'll never know," she says.

You walk back together through the dark, and neither of you looks behind you at the footprints in the snow.
